note: Scenarios for `npm run helper:bench` — B1744, expanded by B1747, WhatsApp-first by B1748. Each block is one situation; the runner expands channels x locales x wordings into cases. Every block's `why` names the ticket or the flow it came from: add a scenario when a conversation fails in front of a person, before arguing about the prompt that caused it.
rules: An expectation must name the failure, not a word near it. `answerHasNot` once matched a sentence that merely stated the address it was using, and scored a correct answer as wrong.

Locales come from the keys of `says`. There is no `hu` here because nobody who has written these speaks Hungarian, and inventing the sentences would put wordings in the instrument that no Hungarian speaker has read. Add them when somebody can.
A refusal scenario matters more than a happy path: a wrong refusal is an annoyance, a missing one is somebody's journal.

Real messages are typed on a phone, one-handed, at the end of a long day. A wording set that is all clean prose is testing a person who does not exist: every scenario carries misspelt and clipped versions of the same intent, and they are expected to pass exactly as the tidy ones do.

Genuinely unclear input is its own scenario, and the right answer there is to ask. A harness that only rewards acting teaches the opposite of what AGENTS.md requires: an empty field beats a plausible fiction, and a confident write from a garbled message is the worst outcome this product has.

A read tool never proposes — it answers with a block. Use `calls` for a read and `proposes` for a write; `proposes` on a read scored 0 of 22 against a product that was doing the right thing every single time.
A scenario that only asserts a refusal never gets `nudges`. Where the right answer is to ask, there is nothing to resolve to, and a nudge would be the benchmark talking itself into a write.

scenarios.author: opus

wanted: sonnet: Listing what is unfinished (`unfinished`) — needs one or more draft days already staged in the world; the runner can only stage trips, not existing days.

sonnet: Asking what a specific day already says (`read_day`) or correcting a day that was already published earlier in a session — needs a pre-written day (title, words, draft/published state) in the world, which is not stageable yet.

sonnet: Listing or revoking an actual invite link (`invites`, `revoke_invite`) — needs a pre-existing invite record (kind, name, created date) in the world; only `share`/`select` for a contact card exist today, not an issued invite.
sonnet: Correcting a photo caption or a day's GPS pin — needs photographs or a location pin staged on a day, which the world schema has no field for.

sonnet: Turning off a trip's cost or coordinate tracking mid-trip (`trip_tracks`) on a trip that already has some days written — needs existing days to make the 'stop asking from now on' framing legible; with only an empty trip the scenario cannot distinguish stopping tracking from never having started.
opus: A day that exists and says one thing while the person insists it says another — the `day` guard (B932) needs a staged day with known prose to check a quote against.
opus: A published day the person asks about after pressing nothing — the `up` guard (B970) is only half testable while the world cannot stage a published day.
opus: A trip with costs in two currencies, one of them without a rate — the `partial` guard (B960) needs staged costs and a `notInTheTotal` to be dropped from.
opus: A credit balance the turn has actually read — the `vague` guard (B1029) needs a staged account balance to catch 'you have credits remaining'.
opus: A photograph in the inbox with no caption and no coordinates — the `onPage` guard (B1563) needs staged files to make 'you'll find the descriptions on the page' false.
opus: An invite already sent but not yet approved, and the person asking whether it worked — needs staged invites to separate 'she can ask to be let in' from 'she can read it'.
opus: A contact row that exists but fails `eligible()` on two gates — the `eligible` guard (B1399) needs staged postcard recipients with their three flags.
opus: A voice note or a shared photograph as the whole message — the commonest real WhatsApp input and the one the runner cannot send at all.
opus: A long gap and a new subject in the same thread — the prompt's 'continue, or fresh' rule needs the runner to stage conversation age, not just turns.
